claim: Roseiflexus castenholzii is a chlorosome-less filamentous anoxygenic photosynthetic bacterium.
source: Roseiflexus (R.) castenholzii is a chlorosome-less filamentous anoxygenic photosynthetic bacterium (Hanada et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation to Hanada et al., 2002.

claim: R. castenholzii contains only one light harvesting complex which forms an unusual RC-LH complex.
source: It contains only one LH, which forms an unusual RC-LH complex.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on established knowledge about this organism.

claim: The R. castenholzii RC-LH complex structurally resembles RC-LH1 but has spectroscopic characteristics similar to the peripheral LH2 of purple bacteria.
source: This complex structurally resembles RC-LH1 but has similar spectroscopic characteristics that are similar to the peripheral LH2 of purple bacteria (Collins et al., 2010; Collins et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Collins et al., 2010 and Collins et al., 2009.

claim: The previously reported cryo-EM structure of R. castenholzii RC-LH was at 4.1 Å resolution.
source: We previously reported the cryo-electron microscopy (EM) structure of R. castenholzii RC-LH at 4.1 Å resolution.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text referring to previous work by the authors.

claim: The R. castenholzii RC-LH structure revealed an RC composed of L, M, and cytochrome c subunits surrounded by an opened elliptical LH ring of 15 LHαβs.
source: It revealed an RC composed of L, M, and cytochrome (cyt) c subunits surrounded by an opened elliptical LH ring of 15 LHαβs, with the tetraheme binding domain of cyt c protruding on the periplasmic side.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text describing the structural features of the complex.

claim: The R. castenholzii RC does not contain an H subunit unlike purple bacteria.
source: The RC is compositionally larger in purple bacteria than in R. castenholzii, in which it does not contain an H subunit (Pugh et al., 1998; Qian et al., 2005; Yamada et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Pugh et al., 1998; Qian et al., 2005; Yamada et al., 2005.

claim: The R. castenholzii RC-LH contains a unique cytochrome c transmembrane helix and subunit X that flank the gap of the LH ring to form a novel quinone shuttling channel.
source: However, it does contain a unique cyt c transmembrane (c-TM) helix and the newly identified subunit X, both of which flank the gap of the LH ring to form a novel quinone shuttling channel (Xin et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Xin et al., 2018.

claim: Pigment analyses revealed a 2:3 Car:BChl molar ratio of R. castenholzii RC-LH.
source: Pigment analyses have revealed a 2:3 Car:BChl molar ratio of R. castenholzii RC-LH (Collins et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Collins et al., 2009.

claim: The previous 4.1 Å cryo-EM structure resolved only one keto-γ-carotene molecule spanning the interface of each LHαβ.
source: However, the cryo-EM structure resolved only one keto-γ-carotene (KγC) molecule spanning the interface of each LHαβ, coordinating two B880s and one additional B800 at the periplasmic and the cytoplasmic side, respectively.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text describing the previous structural findings.

claim: Cryo-EM structures of native RC-LH complexes were determined at 2.8 Å, 3.1 Å, and 2.9 Å resolutions from cells grown under high, medium, and low illuminations respectively.
source: We here determined cryo-EM structures of native RC-LH (nRC-LH) complexes purified from R. castenholzii cells grown under high (180 μmol m–2 s–1), medium (32 μmol m–2 s–1), and low (2 μmol m–2 s–1) illuminations at 2.8 Å, 3.1 Å, and 2.9 Å resolutions, respectively.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and represents experimental data from the study.

claim: All three nRC-LH structures from different light intensities shared the same architecture.
source: All three structures shared the same architecture, indicating that the Car composition and assembly are not affected by light intensities.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and based on structural comparison data from the study.

claim: 14 additional KγC molecules were identified in the exterior of the LH ring (KγCext) in the high-resolution structures.
source: From these high-resolution structures, we identified 14 additional KγC molecules in the exterior of the LH ring (KγCext).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and represents new structural data from the study.

claim: The newly identified KγCext molecules in combination with B800 blocked the proposed quinone channel between LHαβ subunits, forming a sealed LH ring conformation.
source: In combination with the B800 on the cytoplasmic side, the newly identified KγCext molecules blocked the proposed quinone channel between LHαβ subunits, forming a sealed LH ring conformation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and based on structural analysis from the study.

claim: The full amino acid sequences of subunit X, TM7, and an additional TM helix derived from hypothetical proteins Y and Z were assigned.
source: We also assigned the full amino acid sequences of subunit X, TM7, and an additional TM helix that were derived from hypothetical proteins Y and Z, respectively, and demonstrated their roles in forming the quinone channel and stabilizing the RC-LH interactions.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and represents new structural assignment data from the study.

claim: A 3.1 Å resolution cryo-EM structure of dRC-LH resolved five KγC molecules bound in the interior of the LH ring (KγCint).
source: To investigate the role of Cars in the assembly of RC-LH, R. castenholzii cells were treated with Car biosynthesis inhibitor diphenylamine (DPA) to produce a dRC-LH; a 3.1 Å resolution cryo-EM structure of this complex resolved five KγC molecules bound in the interior of the LH ring (KγCint).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and represents experimental data from the study.

claim: The dRC-LH lacked subunit X and exterior KγC (KγCext) molecules.
source: The absence of subunit X and exterior KγC (KγCext) molecules in the dRC-LH produced an LH ring with exposed LHαβ interface and a larger opening than that of nRC-LH.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and based on structural comparison data from the study.

claim: The dRC-LH conformation accelerated the in vitro quinone/quinol exchange rate of menaquinone-4.
source: This conformation accelerated the in vitro quinone/quinol exchange rate of menaquinone-4, an analog of the native menaquinone-11, but did not affect the Car-to-BChl energy transfer efficiency of dRC-LH.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and based on experimental measurements from the study.

claim: Car depletion did not affect the Car-to-BChl energy transfer efficiency of dRC-LH.
source: This conformation accelerated the in vitro quinone/quinol exchange rate of menaquinone-4, an analog of the native menaquinone-11, but did not affect the Car-to-BChl energy transfer efficiency of dRC-LH.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and based on experimental measurements from the study.

claim: Carotenoids play important roles in light harvesting, photoprotection, and assembly of functional pigment-protein complexes in photosynthesis.
source: Carotenoid (Car) pigments perform central roles in photosynthesis-related light harvesting (LH), photoprotection, and assembly of functional pigment-protein complexes.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: Cars capture blue-green light (450–550 nm) and transfer it to chlorophyll or bacteriochlorophyll in the LH antenna.
source: Specifically, Cars capture blue-green light (450–550 nm) and transfer it to chlorophyll or bacteriochlorophyll ((B)Chl) in the LH antenna.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and represents established knowledge about carotenoid function.

claim: Car-BChl interactions are essential for assembling functional LH complexes in anoxygenic photosynthetic bacteria.
source: In anoxygenic photosynthetic bacteria (PSB), Car-BChl interactions are essential for assembling the functional LH complexes (Davidson and Cogdell, 1981; Hashimoto et al., 2016; Lang and Hunter, 1994; Walz and Ghosh, 1997).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The purple bacterium Rhodobacter sphaeroides contains a closed LH2 ring comprising nine αβ-polypeptides.
source: The well-studied purple bacterium Rhodobacter (Rba.) sphaeroides contains a closed LH2 ring comprising nine αβ-polypeptides; each LHαβ non-covalently binds three BChls (two B850s and one B800) and one Car (Qian et al., 2021b).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Qian et al., 2021b.

claim: Car-less strains of Rba. sphaeroides are unable to assemble an LH2 complex.
source: The Car-less strains of Rba. sphaeroides are unable to assemble an LH2 complex, indicating that Car-BChl interactions are essential for the maintenance of LH2 structural stability (Lang et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Lang et al., 1995.

claim: In the LH1 ring of Rba. sphaeroides, a combination of two Car groups forms a tightly sealed, impenetrable fence-like structure that blocks the proposed quinone channel of the closed ring.
source: In the LH1 ring of Rba. sphaeroides, a combination of two Car groups forms a tightly sealed, impenetrable fence-like structure that blocks the proposed quinone channel of the closed ring (Olsen et al., 2017; Qian et al., 2021c).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Olsen et al., 2017 and Qian et al., 2021c.

claim: In Thermochromatium tepidum and Rhodospirillum rubrum, there are small gaps in the LH1 structure that allow quinones to shuttle across the ring.
source: However, there are fewer Cars in most LH1 structures, so in Thermochromatium (Tch.) tepidum and Rhodospirillum (Rsp.) rubrum for example, there are small gaps that allow quinones to shuttle cross the ring (Niwa et al., 2014; Qian et al., 2021a; Yu et al., 2018b).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Niwa et al., 2014; Qian et al., 2021a; Yu et al., 2018b.

claim: A point mutation in LHα (W24F) dramatically reduces the amounts of LH1-bound Car.
source: A point mutation in LHα (W24F) dramatically reduces the amounts of LH1-bound Car.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: The W24F mutation in the pufX knockout strain of Rba. sphaeroides promotes photosynthetic growth.
source: However, in the pufX knockout strain of Rba. sphaeroides, which possesses a closed LH1 ring composed of 17 LHαβs, the same mutation promotes photosynthetic growth (Cao et al., 2022; McGlynn et al., 1994; Olsen et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Cao et al., 2022; McGlynn et al., 1994; Olsen et al., 2017.

claim: R. castenholzii cells were cultured anaerobically under high, medium, and low illuminations.
source: To investigate the LH-bound Car numbers and its correlation with the light intensities, we anaerobically cultured R. castenholzii cells under the light intensity (32 μmol m–2 s–1) used for obtaining the reported 4.1 Å RC-LH structure (Xin et al., 2018), and also a high and a low light intensity at 180 μmol m–2 s–1 and 2 μmol m–2 s–1, respectively.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and describes the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: The cell proliferation rate was much faster under high illumination than under medium and low illuminations.
source: The cell proliferation rate was much faster under high illumination than that grown under medium and low illuminations, and the cells grown showed a darker reddish-brown color after 120 hr of culturing (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: UV-visible-near infrared spectrophotometry of the isolated nRC-LH complexes showed typical Qy bands at 800 nm (B800) and 880 nm (B880) and a Qx band at 594 nm.
source: Ultraviolet (UV)-visible-near infrared (NIR) spectrophotometry of the isolated nRC-LH complexes showed typical Qy bands at 800 nm (B800) and 880 nm (B880) and a Qx band at 594 nm, which corresponded to LH-bound BChls.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and represents spectroscopic data from the study.

claim: Car-associated absorption peaks were detected at 457 nm, 482 nm, and 519 nm in the nRC-LH complexes.
source: Notably, Car-associated absorption peaks were detected at 457 nm, 482 nm, and 519 nm (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The nRC-LH complexes purified from cells under high, medium, and low illuminations showed the same Car absorption spectrum.
source: The nRC-LH complexes purified from cells under high, medium, and low illuminations showed the same Car absorption spectrum (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E), indicating the pigments content was not affected by light intensities.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Superposition of the high illumination model with that of medium and low illumination gave root mean square deviation of 1.753 Å and 1.765 Å, respectively.
source: Superposition of the high illumination model with that of medium and low illumination gave root mean square deviation of 1.753 Å and 1.765 Å, respectively, indicating these three structures share the same architecture, and light intensities did not affect the conformation of the nRC-LH structures.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and represents structural comparison data from the study.

claim: The 15 LHαβ heterodimers formed an opened elliptical ring surrounding the RC with long and short axes of 112 Å and 103 Å, respectively.
source: The 15 LHαβ heterodimers formed an opened elliptical ring surrounding the RC, which contained L, M, and cyt c subunits; the long and short axes were 112 Å and 103 Å, respectively, and a tetraheme binding domain of cyt c protruded into the periplasmic space (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 1A and B.

claim: The RC contained a photo-reactive special pair of BChls, one accessory BChl, three bacteriopheophytins, two MQ-11 (MQA and MQB) and a newly identified MQc, and an iron atom.
source: Similar as most purple bacteria, the RC contained a photo-reactive special pair of BChls, one accessory BChl, three bacteriopheophytins (BPheos), two MQ-11 (MQA and MQB) and a newly identified MQc, and an iron atom to mediate the charge separation and subsequent electron transfer (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 1C.

claim: Each LHαβ non-covalently bound two B880s and one B800 BChl on the periplasmic and cytoplasmic sides.
source: Each LHαβ non-covalently bound two B880s and one B800 BChl on the periplasmic and cytoplasmic sides (Figures 1C and 2A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figures 1C and 2A.

claim: The LH ring bound 15 KγCint, 14 KγCext Cars, and an additional KγC that inserted between the LHαβ1 and c-TM in all three structures.
source: In particular, the LH ring bound 15 KγCint, 14 KγCext Cars, and an additional KγC that inserted between the LHαβ1 and c-TM in all three structures (Figure 1B–D, Figure 1—figure supplement 5, Video 1), indicating both Car compositions and assembly in the nRC-LH were not affected by light intensities.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figure 1B–D, Figure 1—figure supplement 5, and Video 1.

claim: Each LHαβ heterodimer of R. castenholzii was stabilized by hydrogen bonding interactions between LHβ-Arg55 and LHα-Asn37 on the periplasmic side, and by LHβ-Gln22 and LHα-Arg4 on the cytoplasmic side.
source: Each LHαβ heterodimer of R. castenholzii was stabilized by hydrogen bonding interactions between LHβ-Arg55 and LHα-Asn37 on the periplasmic side, and by LHβ-Gln22 and LHα-Arg4 on the cytoplasmic side (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The B800 porphyrin ring in R. castenholzii was inclined nearly 60° relative to the G. phototrophica LHh-bound B800.
source: Superposition of each LHαβ with that of G. phototrophica LHh revealed high overlap at the TM helices, with the exception that the B800 porphyrin ring was inclined nearly 60° relative to the G. phototrophica LHh-bound B800 (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2B.

claim: Compared to Tch. tepidum RC-LH1, the B800s in R. castenholzii occupied the space of an N-terminal helix of LH1-α and the head of a ubiquinone bound in the LHαβ interface.
source: Compared to Tch. tepidum RC-LH1 that contains a closed LH1 ring, the B800s occupied the space of an N-terminal helix of LH1-α and the head of an ubiquinone (UQ) bound in the LHαβ interface (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2C.

claim: 15 KγCint molecules obliquely spanned the LHαβ subunits, with the 4-oxo-β-ionone rings sandwiched between adjacent LHαβs and the ψ-end groups directed into the LH center.
source: 15 KγCint molecules obliquely spanned the LHαβ subunits, with the 4-oxo-β-ionone rings sandwiched between adjacent LHαβs and the ψ-end groups directed into the LH center.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and describes structural features observed in the study.

claim: 14 KγC were detected in a second position in the LH ring exterior (KγCext), which were almost parallel to the adjacent LHβ subunits.
source: In addition, another 14 KγC were detected in a second position in the LH ring exterior (KγCext), which were almost parallel to the adjacent LHβ subunits; the 4-oxo-β-ionone rings were directed toward the cytoplasmic side and the ψ-end groups stretched into the periplasm (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2D.

claim: A newly identified KγC was sandwiched between LHαβ1 and c-TM, with its 4-oxo-β-ionone ring directing toward the RC-Y subunit.
source: Alternatively, a newly identified KγC was sandwiched between LHαβ1 and c-TM, with its 4-oxo-β-ionone ring directing toward the RC-Y subunit (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2E.

claim: The B-factor was higher for KγCext than for KγCint molecules, with the latter having lower conformational flexibility.
source: The B-factor was higher for KγCext than for KγCint molecules, with the latter having lower conformational flexibility (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Identification of these Cars yielded in a Car:BChl ratio of approximately 1:1.6 for the nRC-LH structure.
source: Identification of these Cars yielded in a Car:BChl ratio of approximately 1:1.6 for the nRC-LH structure; this was consistent with results from previous pigment studies (Collins et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Collins et al., 2009.

claim: HPLC-mass spectrometry analyses of the pigments in nRC-LH revealed a typical BChl peak at the retention time of 5.58 min, and several peaks of γ-carotene and its derivatives.
source: High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)-mass spectrometry (MS) analyses of the pigments in nRC-LH revealed a typical BChl peak at the retention time of 5.58 min, and several peaks of γ-carotene and its derivatives (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The nRC-LH resembled Rba. sphaeroides RC-LH1, which also binds two groups of Cars with different configurations.
source: The nRC-LH thus resembled Rba. sphaeroides RC-LH1, which also binds two groups of Cars with different configurations (Tani et al., 2021b).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Tani et al., 2021b.

claim: The keto groups of both Car types in nRC-LH were shifted toward the LHα subunits by ~6.7 Å compared to Rba. sphaeroides RC-LH1.
source: Superposition analyses revealed similar Car positions and orientations between these two structures, although the keto groups of both Car types in nRC-LH were shifted toward the LHα subunits by ~6.7 Å (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A and C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figure 2—figure supplement 4A and C.

claim: The KγCext molecules and additional B800s in R. castenholzii nRC-LH together blocked the LHαβ interface.
source: As a result, the KγCext molecules and additional B800s in R. castenholzii nRC-LH together blocked the LHαβ interface (Figure 2F), which serves as the quinone channel for the closed LH1 ring (Qian et al., 2022; Yu et al., 2018b), and for the opened LH1 ring bound only with interior Cars (Qian et al., 2021a; Swainsbury et al., 2021; Yu et al., 2018b).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2F and multiple citations.

claim: Subunit X in R. castenholzii was an independent TM helix that did not show any spatial overlap with PufX and PufY from the monomeric Rba. sphaeroides RC-LH1.
source: Unlike the Rba. sphaeroides RC-LH1 protein PufX, which interacts with both LH1 and the L and H subunits of the RC (Cao et al., 2022; Tani et al., 2022a), subunit X in R. castenholzii was an independent TM helix that did not show any spatial overlap with PufX and PufY from the monomeric Rba. sphaeroides RC-LH1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 4E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 4E and citations.

claim: The amino acid sequence (Met1-Ser26) for subunit X was successfully assigned from the high-resolution structure of nRC-LH.
source: From the high-resolution structure of nRC-LH, we successfully assigned the amino acid sequence (Met1-Ser26) for subunit X, which was derived from a hypothetical protein containing 32 amino acid residues (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figure 2G and H.

claim: Subunit X was encoded by coding sequences (CDS: 1,060,366–1,060,464) in R. castenholzii (strain DSM 13941/HLO8) genome.
source: This polypeptide was encoded by coding sequences (CDS: 1,060,366–1,060,464) in R. castenholzii (strain DSM 13941/HLO8) genome, but it was not annotated in the Protein Database of Uniprot and NCBI.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and represents genomic data from the study.

claim: The amino acid sequence of subunit X showed strict conservation with a hypothetical protein KatS3mg058_1126 from Roseiflexus sp.
source: The amino acid sequence of subunit X showed strict conservation with a hypothetical protein KatS3mg058_1126 (GenBank: GIV99722.1) from Roseiflexus sp., which was denoted by metagenomic analyses of the uncultivated bacteria in Katase hot spring sediment (Kato et al., 2022; Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 5 and a citation to Kato et al., 2022.

claim: A weak hydrogen bond (3.5 Å) formed between the Met25 main chain nitrogen of subunit X and Arg19 amino nitrogen of c-TM.
source: A weak hydrogen bond (3.5 Å) formed between the Met25 main chain nitrogen of subunit X and Arg19 amino nitrogen of c-TM.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and represents structural data from the study.

claim: R. castenholzii L and M subunits are encoded by a fused gene puf LM but processed into two independent peptides in the complex.
source: Unlike purple bacteria, R. castenholzii L and M subunits are encoded by a fused gene puf LM but processed into two independent peptides in the complex (Collins et al., 2010; Collins et al., 2009; Yamada et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Collins et al., 2010; Collins et al., 2009; Yamada et al., 2005.

claim: RC-L subunit contains TM1-5 and terminates at Ala315, whereas the TM6-10 composed RC-M starts from Pro335.
source: In current model, RC-L subunit contains TM1-5 and terminates at Ala315, whereas the TM6-10 composed RC-M starts from Pro335 (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: R. castenholzii RC-L contains an N-terminal extension (Met1-Pro35) that was solvent exposed on the cytoplasmic side.
source: In addition, R. castenholzii RC-L contains an N-terminal extension (Met1-Pro35) that was solvent exposed on the cytoplasmic side (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and C.

claim: A separate TM helix was resolved with amino acid residues (Met1-Pro32) from a hypothetical protein Y.
source: Near the TM5 from RC-L and c-TM, a separate TM helix (corresponding to the TM7 in previous 4.1 Å model) was resolved with amino acid residues (Met1-Pro32) from a hypothetical protein Y (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 3C.

claim: Protein Y was encoded by CDS (1,089,483–1,089,602) from R. castenholzii (strain DSM 13941/HLO8) genomic DNA.
source: Similar as subunit X, this protein was encoded by CDS (1,089,483–1,089,602) from R. castenholzii (strain DSM 13941/HLO8) genomic DNA, but it was not annotated in Protein Database as well.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and represents genomic data from the study.

claim: The amino acid sequence of protein Y was conserved with a hypothetical protein KatS3mg058_1154 from Roseiflexus sp.
source: Coincidently, the amino acid sequence of protein Y was conserved with a hypothetical protein KatS3mg058_1154 (GenBank: GIV99750.1) from Roseiflexus sp. (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: An individual TM helix was identified between the LHα11 and RC-M, which was assigned to cover the amino acid residues Ser12 to Asn58 of a hypothetical protein (WP_041331144.1) from R. castenholzii, named protein Z.
source: Unlike purple bacteria, R. castenholzii RC does not contain an H subunit. Instead, we identified an individual TM helix between the LHα11 and RC-M (Figures 1B and 3D–E). Superposition revealed mismatch of this TM helix with that of the purple bacterial H subunit (Figure 3A). This helix was assigned to cover the amino acid residues Ser12 to Asn58 of a hypothetical protein (WP_041331144.1) from R. castenholzii (strain DSM 13941/HLO8) (Figure 3D), we named it protein Z.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figures 1B, 3A, 3D, and 3E.

claim: Protein Z was verified with a sequence coverage of 19% by peptide mass fingerprinting analyses of the blue-native PAGE of the nRC-LH.
source: This protein was verified with a sequence coverage of 19% by peptide mass fingerprinting (PMF) analyses of the blue-native PAGE of the nRC-LH (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Table 1.

claim: R. castenholzii cyt c contains an N-terminal transmembrane helix c-TM, which was absent in G. phototrophica and Tch. tepidum RC-bound cyt c.
source: In contrast with most purple bacteria, R. castenholzii cyt c contains an N-terminal transmembrane helix c-TM, which was absent in G. phototrophica and Tch. tepidum RC-bound cyt c, and was even distinct from Rpi. globiformis cyt c that also conains an N-terminal TM helix (Tani et al., 2022b; Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, Figure 3—figure supplement 3, and a citation to Tani et al., 2022b.

claim: Several structured lipids (phosphatidylglycerol, PG, and diglyceride, DG) were identified within the interface between the RC and LH subunits.
source: We also identified several structured lipids (phosphatidylglycerol, PG, and diglyceride, DG) within the interface between the RC and LH subunits (Figure 3G and H), these protein-lipids contacts further stabilized the nRC-LH complex.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figure 3G and H.

claim: DPA treatment of R. castenholzii cells decreased the proliferation rate of cells grown under high illumination.
source: In response to DPA treatment, bacterial growth curves clearly indicated a decreased proliferation rate of cells grown under high illumination, confirming the important roles of Cars in photosynthesis and cell proliferation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: DPA treatment did not affect the growth of cells under medium and low illuminations.
source: Interestingly, DPA treatment did not affect the growth of cells under medium and low illuminations, which showed an overall much lower proliferation rate (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The color of the growing cells changed progressively from brownish red in the first culture to light yellow in the fifth sub-culture in response to DPA treatment.
source: Concomitantly, the color of the growing cells changed progressively from brownish red in the first culture to light yellow in the fifth sub-culture (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), indicating gradual inhibition of Car biosynthesis during sub-culturing.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: There was a striking decrease in Car absorbance in dRC-LH complexes extracted from the third through fifth sub-cultures of DPA-treated cells compared to nRC-LH extracted from untreated cells.
source: There was a striking decrease in Car absorbance in dRC-LH complexes extracted from the third through fifth sub-cultures of DPA-treated cells compared to nRC-LH extracted from untreated cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: HPLC analysis of dRC-LH isolated from the fifth sub-culture of DPA-treated cells showed same pigment compositions but strikingly decreased Car absorbance compared to the nRC-LH.
source: Additionally, HPLC analysis of dRC-LH isolated from the fifth sub-culture of DPA-treated cells showed same pigment compositions but strikingly decreased Car absorbance compared to the nRC-LH (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The cryo-EM structure of dRC-LH isolated from the fifth sub-culture of DPA-treated R. castenholzii cells was determined at 3.1 Å resolution.
source: To illustrate the effects of DPA treatment on the RC-LH architecture, we determined the cryo-EM structure of dRC-LH isolated from the fifth sub-culture of DPA-treated R. castenholzii cells at 3.1 Å resolution (Figure 4A and B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figure 4A and B, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The most obvious difference between nRC-LH and dRC-LH structures was the absence of the entire X subunit and the cytoplasmic region of cyt c subunit (Pro6-Val16) in the dRC-LH.
source: The most obvious difference between these two structures was the absence of the entire X subunit and the cytoplasmic region of cyt c subunit (Pro6-Val16) in the dRC-LH; both were located at the LH opening of nRC-LH (Figure 4C, Video 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 6C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figure 4C, Video 2, and Figure 1—figure supplement 6C.

claim: Only five KγCint molecules that spanned the LHαβ5, -7, -9, -10, and -11 heterodimers were resolved with clear density maps in the dRC-LH structure.
source: Notably, only five KγCint molecules that spanned the LHαβ5, -7, -9, -10, and -11 heterodimers were resolved with clear density maps and built in the dRC-LH structure, whereas none of the KγCext molecules were observed (Figure 4B, Figure 1—figure supplement 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, Video 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figure 4B, Figure 1—figure supplement 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, and Video 1.

claim: The five KγCint molecules in dRC-LH adopted the same conformation and a similar edge-to-edge distance from LH-bound B800/B880s as the corresponding KγCint molecules did in nRC-LH.
source: Additionally, the five KγCint molecules in dRC-LH adopted the same conformation and a similar edge-to-edge distance from LH-bound B800/B880s as the corresponding KγCint molecules did in nRC-LH (Figure 4D, Tables 3 and 4).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figure 4D, Tables 3 and 4.

claim: Car depletion did not affect the LHαβ structure.
source: These observations thus indicated that Car depletion did not affect the LHαβ structure.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and based on structural comparison data from the study.

claim: The distances between adjacent LHαs and LHβs in the dRC-LH showed average increases of 0.5 Å and 1.0 Å, respectively, compared with nRC-LH.
source: Nevertheless, the distances between adjacent LHαs and LHβs in the dRC-LH showed average increases of 0.5 Å and 1.0 Å, respectively, compared with nRC-LH (Table 5).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Table 5.

claim: The Mg-to-Mg distances between adjacent B880s and B800s increased in dRC-LH.
source: Accordingly, the Mg-to-Mg distances between adjacent B880s and B800s also increased in dRC-LH (Tables 6 and 7).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Tables 6 and 7.

claim: The LH-bound B880s and B800s shifted away from the LH ring center by ~2.0 Å in dRC-LH.
source: Specifically, the LH-bound B880s and B800s shifted away from the LH ring center by ~2.0 Å, consequently increasing the Mg-to-Mg distance between LH-bound B880s and the nearest special pair of BChls in the RC (Figure 4E, Table 8).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figure 4E and Table 8.

claim: In nRC-LH, the c-TM and subunit X were positioned to the sides of LHα1 and LHβ15, respectively, forming a 19.4 Å gap between the c-TM and LHα15, and a 28 Å gap between subunit X and LHβ1.
source: The c-TM was closer to LHα1 (9.7 Å) than to LHα15, whereas subunit X was closer to LHβ15 (11.2 Å), creating a narrow gap between the c-TM and the LHαβ15 (Figure 4C and F, Table 5). The B800 pigment was not detected between c-TM and LHα15 (Figure 4C). Thus, the c-TM and subunit X were positioned to the sides of LHα1 and LHβ15, respectively; this formed a 19.4 Å gap between the c-TM and LHα15, and a 28 Å gap between subunit X and LHβ1, both of which may have allowed reduced quinones to exit the LH to the membrane quinone pool.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figure 4C and F, and Table 5.

claim: Because dRC-LH lacked subunit X, the gap between LHβ1 and LHβ15 increased to ~38.0 Å.
source: Because dRC-LH lacked subunit X, the gap between LHβ1 and LHβ15 increased to ~38.0 Å (Figure 4C and F).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figure 4C and F.

claim: The initial oxidation rate of Ac was markedly higher in the presence of dRC-LH than nRC-LH.
source: The initial oxidation rate of Ac was markedly higher in the presence of dRC-LH than nRC-LH (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 4H.

claim: dRC-LH had an accelerated quinone/quinol exchange rate of menaquinone-4 at 6.12±0.62 μM min–1.
source: This was consistent with the determined apparent Michaelis constants, which showed that dRC-LH had an accelerated quinone/quinol exchange rate of menaquinone-4 at 6.12±0.62 μM min–1 (Table 9).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Table 9.

claim: In the absence of KγCext, the head of each KγCint molecule shifted toward the B800 porphyrin ring, which moved the head out from the center of the LH ring by ~3.0 Å.
source: Thus, in the absence of KγCext, the head of each KγCint molecule shifted toward the B800 porphyrin ring, which moved the head out from the center of the LH ring by ~3.0 Å (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 5B.

claim: The edge-to-edge distances of KγCint to the B800/B880s remained similar between dRC-LH and nRC-LH.
source: However, the edge-to-edge distances of KγCint to the B800/B880s remained similar between dRC-LH and nRC-LH (Table 3).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Table 3.

claim: Excitation of nRC-LH at 470 nm yielded emissions at 900 nm, whereas dRC-LH excitation produced emissions at 905 nm.
source: Excitation of nRC-LH at 470 nm yielded emissions at 900 nm, whereas dRC-LH excitation produced emissions at 905 nm (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 5C.

claim: The Car-to-BChl energy transfer efficiency remained similar between nRC-LH (44%) and dRC-LH (46%).
source: The results revealed that the Car-to-BChl energy transfer efficiency remained similar between nRC-LH (44%) and dRC-LH (46%) (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 5D.

claim: Each KγC in R. castenholzii contains 11 conjugated double bonds.
source: In R. castenholzii, each KγC contains 11 conjugated double bonds (Collins et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Collins et al., 2009.

claim: Genetic depletion of the LH1-bound Cars promoted the photosynthetic growth of a PufX-knockout Rba. sphaeroides mutant with a closed LH1 ring.
source: Genetic depletion of the LH1-bound Cars promoted the photosynthetic growth of a PufX-knockout Rba. sphaeroides mutant with a closed LH1 ring (Cao et al., 2022; McGlynn et al., 1994; Olsen et al., 2017); this implies that disruption of Cars binding exposed the blocked quinone channel between LHαβ interface and facilitated the quinone exchange, thus promoting photosynthetic growth.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Cao et al., 2022; McGlynn et al., 1994; Olsen et al., 2017.

claim: The open form of the Rhodopseudomonas palustris RC-LH1 has a faster UQ2 diffusion rate than the closed form.
source: This was consistent with a previous observation that the open form of the Rhodopseudomonas (Rps.) palustris RC-LH1 has a faster UQ2 diffusion rate than the closed form (Swainsbury et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Swainsbury et al., 2021.

claim: Cars contribute to the self-assemble of natural α/β polypeptides to form LH1 complexes in vitro.
source: Cars contribute to the self-assemble of natural α/β polypeptides to form LH1 complexes in vitro (Fiedor et al., 2004), Car-less Rsp. rubrum LH1 can be obtained by exogenous recombination (Parkes-Loach et al., 1988).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Fiedor et al., 2004 and Parkes-Loach et al., 1988.

claim: In the Car-less Rba. sphaeroides mutant strain R26, the polymerized form of RC-LH is predominantly monomeric, and the curvature of the photosynthetic membrane is altered due to the lack of dimeric RC-LH.
source: In the Car-less Rba. sphaeroides mutant strain R26, the polymerized form of RC-LH is predominantly monomeric, and the curvature of the photosynthetic membrane is altered due to the lack of dimeric RC-LH (Ng et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Ng et al., 2011.

claim: DPA is a broad-spectrum inhibitor that slows cellular metabolic processes and specifically affects Car biosynthesis by inhibiting phytoene desaturase (CrtI).
source: DPA is a broad-spectrum inhibitor that slows cellular metabolic processes and specifically affects Car biosynthesis by inhibiting phytoene desaturase (CrtI), an essential enzyme catalyzes conversion of the colorless Car precursor phytoene to the colored lycopene (Bramley, 1993).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Bramley, 1993.

claim: DPA treatment dramatically decreased the R. castenholzii proliferation rate and depleted the LH-bound Cars in dRC-LH.
source: We here found that DPA treatment not only dramatically decreased the R. castenholzii proliferation rate but also depleted the LH-bound Cars in dRC-LH (Figures 1A and 4, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Figures 1A and 4, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: R. castenholzii forms the deepest branch of photosynthetic bacteria.
source: Here, we analyzed native RC-LH (nRC-LH) and Car-depleted RC-LH (dRC-LH) complexes in Roseiflexus castenholzii, a chlorosome-less filamentous anoxygenic phototroph that forms the deepest branch of photosynthetic bacteria.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the abstract.

claim: The space between the LHαβ subunits can serve as quinone exchange channel for the closed LH1 ring.
source: Therefore, the space between the LHαβ subunits can serve as quinone exchange channel for the closed LH1 ring (Qian et al., 2022; Yu et al., 2018b), and also for the opened LH1 ring bound only with interior Cars (Qian et al., 2021a; Swainsbury et al., 2021; Yu et al., 2018b).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by multiple citations.

claim: For Tch. tepidum RC-LH1 that contains an almost symmetric and completely closed LH1 ring, one UQ8 was found to be inserted between the LH1α and LH1β subunits.
source: For Tch. tepidum RC-LH1 that contains an almost symmetric and completely closed LH1 ring, except the 'waiting' UQ8 identified near QB, one UQ8 was found to be inserted between the LH1α and LH1β subunits (Yu et al., 2018a), representing a potential quinone exchange channel between the LHαβ interface.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Yu et al., 2018a.
